answer.text: I don't have enough in this dataset to answer that precisely. From what's here, the portfolio is mixed: a few markets are tracking below forecast while others are growing. Try asking about a specific market, region, or KPI.

Six markets are flagged in the data. Germany is the clearest concern: it's at risk, below forecast and down year on year, with a sharp dip in March. Spain is off track, and Italy, the United Kingdom, France and Brazil are at risk. The other seven markets are on track.

As of May 2026, all five of Europe's markets are flagged in the data. Germany and Spain are off track, and Italy, the United Kingdom and France are at risk. Germany is furthest under forecast at 92.0% attainment, then Italy at 93.0%, the United Kingdom at 94.3% and France at 96.4%. Spain's flag sits oddly with its 104.5% attainment, so check its source row.
{market}'s revenue in {period} was {actual} against a {forecast} forecast, {attainment} attainment{mom}.

Germany's revenue fell in early 2026, with the steepest drop in March. The decline runs across the product portfolio there, and actuals came in well under forecast for those months, which is what pulled the market into off-track territory. It has steadied since, but is still tracking below the prior year.

APAC is outgrowing Europe in May 2026. Its revenue is up 11.5% year on year and sits at 104.9% of forecast, against 1.7% growth and 95.4% for Europe. China and Japan lead APAC, while Germany and Italy are furthest under plan in Europe.

The portfolio is not missing forecast: it is at 100.4% of forecast in May 2026. The shortfall is in individual markets. Germany (92.0%), Italy (93.0%) and the United Kingdom (94.3%) are furthest under plan, while APAC runs ahead at 104.9%. I can't attribute the gaps further from this data alone, since it doesn't break out the drivers behind each market's forecast, so treat this as directional.

I can't answer that. The dataset only covers actuals and forecasts through the current horizon, which ends 2026-05, so I have no basis for projecting past it. If forward forecast data is loaded, I can summarise it.

Here's the portfolio at a glance.

Overall the book is mixed but broadly stable. Total revenue in the latest period is up against the prior year, carried by APAC and North America. North America remains the anchor: the United States is the single largest market and is tracking on plan, with Canada steady behind it.

APAC is the growth story. China and Japan are both well ahead of forecast and growing strongly year on year, and India is improving off a smaller base. Australia is roughly flat but on plan.

Europe is the soft spot. Germany fell sharply in early 2026, worst in March, and is still below the prior year despite steadying; Italy is tracking under forecast; the United Kingdom, France, and Spain are close to plan. LATAM is split, with Mexico steady and Brazil's growth stalled.

In short: APAC and North America are doing the work, Europe is the drag, and the markets to watch are Germany, Italy, and Brazil. Ask me about any of them for the detail behind these numbers.
